key_insight: OMatG-FC generates new inorganic crystals by learning atomic species and cell volume within fixed structural frameworks, achieving a reported state-of-the-art stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) rate below the convex hull.
engineering_relevance: Conditioning on existing atomic arrangements reduces generation dimensionality and offers a route to materials discovery without learning atomic packings from scratch.
method: Fix fractional atomic coordinates and unit-volume lattice vectors to define each framework.
Use discrete flow matching for atomic species and stochastic interpolants for cell-volume scaling.
Analyze duplicate frameworks in MP-20 and provide a framework-split dataset.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses LeMat-GenBench with three machine-learning interatomic potentials; the abstract reports state-of-the-art S.U.N. performance but gives no numerical rates.
watch_item: Fixed frameworks restrict exploration of new atomic packings, and predicted stability still requires validation beyond machine-learning interatomic potentials.
